body:
### Problem

`\%C` skips the composing characters after the previous atom (`:h /\%C`), so `a\%C` matches
"a" followed by U+0300 COMBINING GRAVE ACCENT. With 'ignorecase' (or `\c`) the backtracking
engine (`'regexpengine'=1`) no longer matches it. The NFA engine and the default `re=0` do.

| pattern on "ca" + U+0300 + "t" | re=1 noic | re=1 ic | re=2 ic |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a\%C` | 1 | **-1** | 1 |
| `\ca\%C` | 1 | **-1** | 1 |
| `ca\%Ct` | 0 | **-1** | 0 |
| `[a]\%C` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `a\Z` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

The cause seems to be `cstrncmp()` (`src/nvim/regexp.c:1753`). In the `EXACTLY` case of
`regmatch()` (`src/nvim/regexp.c:6745`), with 'ignorecase' the literal is compared with
`cstrncmp()`, which counts characters with `MB_PTR_ADV()`. That steps over a character
*including* its composing characters, so the pattern's "a" (1 byte) is compared with
"a" + U+0300 (3 bytes) and the comparison fails before `RE_COMPOSING` gets a chance to skip
the accent. Without 'ignorecase' only the first byte is compared, and the composing check
right after it already makes an exception for `OP(next) == RE_COMPOSING`.

Collections (`[a]\%C`) do not use `cstrncmp()` and `\Z` takes its fallback path, so both
work.

Found by differential fuzzing of the two engines (libFuzzer harness that runs every pattern on
both and compares the first match). Vim has the same code and the same result (vim/vim#NNNN).

A possible fix is to count code points instead of characters-with-composing in the
'ignorecase' branch of `cstrncmp()`, so composing characters are handled the same way as
without 'ignorecase' (by the check in the `EXACTLY` case, which already respects `\%C`):

```c
    // count the number of characters for byte-length of s1
    while (n1 > 0 && *p != NUL) {
      n1 -= utf_ptr2len(p);
      p += utf_ptr2len(p);
      n2++;
    }
    // count the number of bytes to advance the same number of chars for s2
    p = s2;
    while (n2-- > 0 && *p != NUL) {
      p += utf_ptr2len(p);
    }
```

Not run against the test suite. The existing `\%C` tests (`test_filter_map.vim`) only use
'noignorecase'.


### Steps to reproduce

```sh
nvim --clean --headless +'set re=1 noic' +"lua print(vim.fn.match('ca\204\128t', [[a\%C]]))" +q
# 1
nvim --clean --headless +'set re=1 ic' +"lua print(vim.fn.match('ca\204\128t', [[a\%C]]))" +q
# -1
nvim --clean --headless +'set re=2 ic' +"lua print(vim.fn.match('ca\204\128t', [[a\%C]]))" +q
# 1
```

(`'ca\204\128t'` is "c", "a", U+0300 in UTF-8, "t". A precomposed "à" (U+00E0) is a
different character and does not show the bug.)

### Expected behavior

`a\%C` matches "a" + U+0300 with 'ignorecase' as well, like it does without 'ignorecase' and
with the NFA engine: `match("càt", 'a\%C')` returns 1 for every value of 're' and 'ic'.


### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-54f94d6fc4 (master); also NVIM v0.12.0-dev (Ubuntu package 0.12.0~ubuntu1+git202601110810-d62bbe24cb)

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

yes, Vim 9.2.1252 and 9.1.2141 (`re=1 ic` gives -1, `re=2 ic` gives 1). Reported as vim/vim#21676.

### Operating system/version

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux 7.0.0-34-generic, x86_64)

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.45.0 (not terminal related, also reproduces with `--headless`)

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-kitty

### Installation

build from repo (master 54f94d6, clang); also Ubuntu system package

labels.description: This issue should be fixed in Vim first.
labels.name: needs:vim-patch

title: regexp: with 'ignorecase' the backtracking engine never matches a literal followed by `\%C`
